walkthroughs.body_html:
Readers, Writers and Texts — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Readers, Writers and Texts brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Readers, Writers and Texts.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term unreliable narrator in 1961?
options: Wayne Booth
Northrop Frye
F R Leavis
Mikhail Bakhtin

mcqs.q: Which Marquez novel exemplifies magic realism?
options: Love in the Time of Cholera
One Hundred Years of Solitude
The Autumn of the Patriarch
Chronicle of a Death Foretold

mcqs.q: What is the dramatic function of a soliloquy?
options: A soliloquy is when characters argue with each other.
It reveals a character's inner thoughts directly to the audience while the character is alone on stage — a convention granting access to private psychology.
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
A soliloquy is any long speech a character gives.
Attributing human emotions or qualities to nature or inanimate objects to reflect a character's feelings or scene's mood (e.g. angry storms during conflict).
It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
Pathetic fallacy is when an argument in a story is weak or sad.

mcqs.q: What is the structural framework of The Canterbury Tales?
options: It is a religious text used in Catholic services.
Pathetic fallacy is when characters cry over silly things.
It is one continuous story told by Chaucer from beginning to end.
A frame narrative — pilgrims travelling to Canterbury tell stories along the way, allowing Chaucer to juxtapose different voices, genres and social classes.
